# Chart index

24 chart types. Open the page for the chart you pick (options and a complete example) before writing code.

### Over time

See how a measure moves, repeats or clusters across days, weeks and months.

| Chart | Function | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Line](charts/line.md) | `lineChart` | One or a few series over time, with a typical-value line and an optional comparison. |
| [Stacked area](charts/area.md) | `areaChart` | Volume over time, split into themes, or the same data as a share of the total. |
| [Sparkline](charts/sparkline.md) | `spark` | A tiny trend with no axes, for tables, tiles and lists. |
| [Calendar](charts/calendar.md) | `calendar` | One cell per day, laid out in weeks, to show rhythm and one-off spikes. |
| [Heatmap](charts/heatmap.md) | `heatmap` | A grid of rows against columns, shaded by value, with clear no-data cells. |
| [Small multiples](charts/small-multiples.md) | markup + `spark` | One mini chart per category on a shared layout, with a detail chart for the one you pick. |

### Comparing

Set one thing against another, in order or step by step.

| Chart | Function | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Grouped bars](charts/bars.md) | `barChart` | Compare two measures side by side per period, with a derived line on top. |
| [Ranked bars](charts/hbars.md) | `hbars` | A top-N list with a bar per row, a detail line and optional click-through. |
| [Waterfall](charts/waterfall.md) | `waterfall` | How a starting number becomes an ending number, step by step. |
| [Diverging bars](charts/diverging-bars.md) | `divergingBars` | What went up and what went down: bars either side of a zero line, biggest rise at the top. |
| [Slope chart](charts/slope.md) | `slope` | Two moments side by side, one line per item, so rises and falls read at a glance. |
| [Bump chart](charts/bump.md) | `bump` | Rank over time: who is first this week, and how each one got there. |

### Spread and relationships

See how values are distributed and whether two measures move together.

| Chart | Function | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Histogram](charts/histogram.md) | `histogram` | How a measure is spread: thread length, thread time or cost per response, in bars. |
| [Box plot](charts/box-plot.md) | `boxPlot` | Compare the spread of a measure across groups: median, quartiles, whiskers and outliers. |
| [Scatter and bubble](charts/scatter.md) | `scatter` | Two measures against each other, one dot per item, with size, groups and a trend line. |

### Parts of a whole

Show what a total is made of and where it goes.

| Chart | Function | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Stacked](charts/stacked.md) | `barChart` | Parts of a whole per period, one stable colour per category. |
| [Donut](charts/donut.md) | `donut` | Share of a total, with the hovered slice read out in the centre. |
| [Treemap](charts/treemap.md) | `treemap` | Area proportional to value, packed into a rectangle. |
| [Flow](charts/flow.md) | `flow` | Where money comes from and where it goes, as proportional ribbons. |
| [Funnel](charts/funnel.md) | `funnel` | A journey where each step can only lose people, with the drop-off between steps. |

### At a glance

Single figures, targets, the words people use and the exact numbers behind them.

| Chart | Function | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Gauge](charts/gauge.md) | `gauge` | Progress against a budget or limit, with the state spelled out in words. |
| [KPI tiles](charts/kpi-tiles.md) | markup + `spark` | Headline numbers with a change and a sparkline, plus a loading skeleton. |
| [Word cloud](charts/word-cloud.md) | `wordCloud` | The words people use most, sized by how often they appear, with optional colour for rising and falling. |
| [Data table](charts/data-table.md) | `dataTable` | The accessible twin of every chart: plain numbers in a real table. |

## Choosing between them

- **Line**: Use it to show how one measure moves over time and to spot the odd month.
- **Grouped bars**: Use it to compare two things per period (money in against money out) and show a third derived number, such as the difference, as a line.
- **Stacked**: Use it to show what a total is made of and how that mix changes over time.
- **Donut**: Use it for a handful of parts that add up to one whole, when the share matters more than the exact amounts.
- **Heatmap**: Use it to spot patterns across two dimensions, such as category against month.
- **Calendar**: Use it for daily values over months, when weekday habits and single heavy days are the story.
- **Treemap**: Use it to show how a whole divides across many categories at once, when you want to see the big pieces at a glance.
- **Sparkline**: Use it beside a number to show direction at a glance.
- **Gauge**: Use it for one value against one target: a budget, a quota, a limit.
- **Waterfall**: Use it to explain a change: opening balance, what came in, what went out, closing balance.
- **Flow**: Use it to show the shape of a budget: income sources on the left, spending categories on the right.
- **Ranked bars**: Use it for rankings with long labels (merchants, products, people) where columns would force tiny rotated text.
- **Small multiples**: Use it instead of one crowded multi-line chart, or whenever series have different scales.
- **KPI tiles**: Use them for the three to eight numbers someone should see first.
- **Data table**: Use it beside any chart as the 'Show as table' view, or on its own when people need exact figures.
- **Histogram**: Use it when an average hides what is happening.
- **Box plot**: Use it to compare distributions side by side, such as the cost of a conversation by theme or the time a conversation takes by week.
- **Word cloud**: Use it for a quick feel of what people are asking about, such as the words in the last 30 days of conversations.
- **Diverging bars**: Use it for change between two periods, such as the themes trending up and down this week compared with last.
- **Stacked area**: Use it when the total and its make-up both matter, such as conversations per week by theme.
- **Scatter and bubble**: Use it to see whether two things move together, such as thread length against cost, and to spot the threads that do not follow the pattern.
- **Bump chart**: Use it when order matters more than size, such as which themes lead the conversation each week.
- **Slope chart**: Use it to compare the same items at two points: this week against last, or the first month against the latest.
- **Funnel**: Use it for a sequence people drop out of: conversations started, answered, rated and rated helpful.
